note: Every number in this file is read from the campaign results, never typed. Regenerate with: uv run python scripts/generate_claims.py

claims.claim: Across 126 deterministic drill runs on the published corpus, 0 capacity-overbooking invariant (N1) violations were observed.
claims.limitation: Deterministic tier only: a fixed policy replaces the model. Proves the kernel and services hold, not that agents behave well. Zero observed is over this corpus at this commit, not a proof of impossibility.

claims.claim: Under 54 injected faults across 36 runs, 0 runs produced a duplicate semantic effect.
claims.limitation: Faults are injected at the tool transport boundary. Faults inside Firestore's own commit path are not simulated.

claims.claim: 67 tool calls returned an existing receipt instead of creating a second effect.
claims.limitation: Counted at the broker; the underlying services enforce it independently.

claims.claim: 24 agent-to-tool calls were denied by the authorization layer across the corpus, including a Dispatch Agent attempt to reach restricted inventory tools.
claims.limitation: These are broker and service-layer denials. The Cloud Run IAM denial is a separate, additional layer verified during deployment.

claims.claim: 126 of 126 scored deterministic drill runs passed every expectation, including the hard invariants N1 through N13.
claims.limitation: Expectations are properties of the outcome, not scenario identifiers.

claims.claim: A cancelled ADK invocation re-invokes an already-committed tool on resume. The observed run made 2 tool calls and produced 1 committed effect, because the semantic action ID was identical and the second call replayed the first call's receipt.
claims.limitation: Observed on google-adk 2.7.1 with an in-memory session service. Two other interruption shapes did not re-invoke; all three are published.

claims.claim: Model Armor matched the published prompt-injection payload family at HIGH confidence via the live sanitizeUserPrompt API.
claims.limitation: One payload family, not a detection rate. Night Shift never relies on Model Armor alone: the Dispatch Agent holds no inventory authority regardless of what any screening layer concludes.

claims.claim: Tampering with a published manifest is detected. Editing the state snapshot, the stored verdict, or the signature each produce a distinct MISMATCH, and an unsigned manifest reports PARTIAL rather than PASS.
claims.limitation: Proves the stored verdict follows from the stored state and that the state was signed by the published key holder. It cannot prove the state describes the physical world.

claims.claim: Evidence manifests are signed with a Cloud KMS asymmetric key (EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256) and verify against the exported public key.
claims.limitation: A local EC key is used as a documented fallback when KMS is unreachable; the backend that actually signed is recorded in the manifest.

claims.claim: Field movements in the demo are simulated. No real biobank samples were moved and no real patient or research data exists anywhere in the fixture.
claims.reproduce: uv run python -c "from fixtures.estate import build_estate; print(build_estate().site)"
claims.limitation: This is a statement of scope, not a measurement. The field simulator refuses to run outside demo, drill, and test namespaces.

claims.claim: Six domain services run on Cloud Run under six distinct Google service accounts, and cross-service run.invoker grants mirror the permission matrix.
claims.limitation: Agents are not registered as managed Agent Registry or Agent Runtime resources; see LIMITATIONS.md.
